title: Canonical free internal-module adjunction and local profinite tuple generators
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the coherent profinite site with the sizes of [def-weil-size-convention], and use its internal module category and section modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The free module on a representable profinite parameter is the existing $A[P]$ of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Write $F_A$ for the composite of the free abelian sheaf functor and the free internal $A$-module functor $A\otimes-$, so that $F_A\dashv U$, where $U$ forgets an internal module to a condensed set. This is the same composite defining $A[P]$, not an alternative free object. For a profinite group $G$ and $n\geq0$, put $P_n=G^n$ (the terminal profinite object when $n=0$), and write $A[\underline G^n]=F_A(\underline{P_n})$. For a profinite $S$ and a tuple $x=(x_i)_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)}$ of continuous maps $S\to G$, define its canonical local generator $[x]\in A[\underline G^n](S)$ to be the component at $S$ of the unit of $F_A\dashv U$ on $\underline{P_n}$, applied to the generalized point $s\mapsto(x_i(s))_i$. These are definitions, with no resolution or exactness assertion.
